task.description:
WF-02 Step 1b -- Design gate for REQ-367's design (lib/letflow/design/req367-cd-qa-deploy.md). Claim this handoff (status IN_PROGRESS). Read the design file directly (not just CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). This is infrastructure design (shell script + GitHub Actions workflow), not Elixir -- apply the same rigor as usual (per WF-02 Step 1b's standard checklist) adapted to this shape: (a) does every REQ-367 acceptance criterion map to a concrete design element -- no TBD/deferrals? (b) is deploy/redeploy-qa.sh's procedure fully specified (each step's purpose, target paths, ordering) without actual bash bodies? (c) is cd.yml's trigger/gate mechanism fully specified, including how it avoids duplicating ci.yml's diff logic, without actual YAML bodies? (d) are error-handling/failure-mode expectations stated (what happens if a step fails, health check fails, etc.) -- not left implicit? (e) are cross-file dependencies listed (what ci.yml change is implied, if any)? (f) is there any actual implementation code (real bash lines, real complete YAML blocks) present rather than structural/procedural description -- FAIL if so, even if a quoted precedent (the real letflow-queue cd.yml, clearly marked as a citation) is present, since that's documentation of an existing file, not new implementation, but check the NEW design sections (\u00a71/\u00a72 for redeploy-qa.sh/cd.yml) do not slip into full code?

One known unusual point to specifically evaluate: the design proposes adding a small artifact-upload step to .github/workflows/ci.yml's existing `changes` job (outside this requirement's own owned_modules of deploy/redeploy-qa.sh and .github/workflows/cd.yml), justified as necessary to satisfy REQ-367's 'reuse the changes job's outputs, no duplicated diff logic' acceptance criterion under a workflow_run cross-workflow trigger. Decide explicitly: is this in-scope scope creep or a legitimate, necessary, minimal touch this requirement's acceptance criteria actually require? State your reasoning either way -- this decision gates whether ELIXIR-DEV touches ci.yml at all in Step 2a.

FAIL immediately on any check failure, no partial credit, per Step 1b's standard hard-gate procedure. Complete the handoff: PASS -> next_action 'Route to ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a)' | FAIL -> next_action 'Rework CODE-DESIGNER', issues listing every failed check by requirement id. Commit the completed handoff JSON on branch feature/WF02-REQ367-20260917 and push.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-367 acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element, no TBD/deferrals
deploy/redeploy-qa.sh's full procedure specified without real bash implementation bodies
cd.yml's trigger/gate mechanism fully specified without real YAML implementation bodies
Error/failure-mode handling stated, not left implicit
Explicit ruling on whether the proposed ci.yml touch is legitimate minimal scope or creep
No implementation code present in the NEW design sections (quoted existing precedent is fine and expected)
